title: Input length scan
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and let $B$ be a natural number with $|y|\le B$. Suppose the initial register contents $v$ satisfy $v(r)\le B$ for every register and $v(r_L)\le |y|$. In the register program with mode $\mathrm{mode}$, there is a run from the length-scan instruction to the first prefix-scan instruction that leaves every register unchanged except $r_L$, which is set to $|y|$; every configuration before the final one satisfies the run guard with bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine N over Boolean input
initial register contents v bounded by B at every register
